assessment.nobel_worthiness: Created the modern field of political economics. They formalised how electoral rules, constitutions, regime type and state capacity shape fiscal policy and growth, and they tested these links empirically with cross-country and historical data. The work links theory and evidence on institutions and development, and it has shaped macroeconomics, public economics and comparative politics.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the core pair, through their joint research programme and the 2000 book Political Economics. Besley's work on state capacity, accountability and fiscal capacity is closely complementary, and the three-person limit fits the evidence well. Others such as Acemoglu, Alesina and Roland are outside this credited list and the list does not settle their claims.
assessment.maturity: The work spans about three decades. Its core results have been replicated and extended, and the field is now standard in graduate training. Timing is not a barrier.
uncertainties: Causal identification of constitutional effects from cross-country data remains debated.
Whether the Committee sees the 2024 institutions prize as having already covered much of this territory.
The relative weight of Besley versus other contributors such as Alesina.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bayesian persuasion introduced a tractable framework for how a sender designs information to influence decisions. It has since become a general tool in information economics, mechanism design, industrial organisation, political economy and finance. The conceptual gain is clear: information structure is treated as a choice variable.
assessment.attribution: Kamenica and Gentzkow originated the persuasion model (2011). Morris, with Bergemann, extended it to information design in games and to robust mechanism design, and he has separate foundational work on global games. Bergemann is a strong alternative to Morris, so the attribution choice is genuinely contestable.
assessment.maturity: Fifteen years of development and widespread application. The conceptual core is established, but some empirical and applied validation is still accumulating.
uncertainties: Whether the Committee prefers the originators (Kamenica, Gentzkow) over the broader information-design group (Bergemann, Morris).
Evidence of real-world application is thinner than the theoretical influence.
Gentzkow's separate empirical work may crowd the attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kiyotaki and Moore (1997) showed how collateral constraints amplify and propagate shocks, giving a dynamic mechanism for credit cycles. It became a foundation for macro-finance and shaped how the 2007–09 crisis was analysed. The ideas were adopted in policy models and in much later work on financial frictions.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore are the clear originators of the collateral-constraint cycle model. Gertler and Gilchrist, with Bernanke (already honoured in 2022), developed the related financial accelerator and could be considered but dilute the attribution. I limit the proposal to two names.
assessment.maturity: Nearly three decades of influence, reinforced by the post-2008 literature. Mature.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize for banking and financial crises may weigh against.
Whether the Committee sees the financial accelerator and collateral-constraint strands as a single contribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal rigidities and the New Keynesian framework are central to how central banks model and conduct monetary policy. The contribution has high influence on theory and practice: staggered pricing and contracts, the interest-rate rule, and microfounded policy analysis.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is the hardest problem. Calvo (1983) and Taylor (1980) supply staggered pricing and contracts, Taylor adds the rule, and Woodford gives the synthesis. Galí, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets and others made major contributions, and the eight credited names exceed the three-person limit.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of development, with extensive policy use and some testing through the 2008 crisis and the post-pandemic inflation episode. Fully mature.
uncertainties: Diffuse credit among many contributors makes any trio contestable.
Criticism of the empirical performance of the framework, notably during and after the financial crisis.
Earlier prizes for related macro work (Lucas, Phelps, Kydland–Prescott, Sargent–Sims) may affect the Committee's appetite.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Assembled long-run tax-record series on top incomes and wealth, which changed the empirical basis of the inequality debate and reshaped public economics and policy discussion. The data contribution is large and the research agenda has been widely followed.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez were the pioneers of the top-income series. Zucman's offshore-wealth work is a distinct and more recent contribution, so I leave him out here. Atkinson, who was a core pioneer, is no longer eligible.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of influence. The data series are widely used, though several of the interpretive claims are still disputed.
uncertainties: The theoretical claims about r>g and the accuracy of wealth-share estimates are contested.
The Committee may value measurement contributions differently from identified causal findings.
Policy prominence may affect how the work is perceived, though it should not enter the merit assessment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Machine learning methods for causal inference (double/debiased ML, causal forests, heterogeneous effects) extended the credibility revolution into high-dimensional settings. They are now used widely across economics and in industry and the other sciences.
assessment.attribution: Chernozhukov and coauthors developed double machine learning, and Athey and Wager developed causal forests and related tools. Credit is shared across a broader community, including Imbens, Belloni and Hansen, who are outside the list. Wager is younger, so I propose the two senior names.
assessment.maturity: The core methods date from about 2014–2018. Adoption is broad but the track record is shorter than for the other candidates.
uncertainties: The work may be too recent for a prize.
Credit is spread over many coauthors.
Imbens was recognised in 2021 for causal-inference methodology, so the Committee may see this as incremental.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hsieh and Klenow (2009) offered a tractable accounting framework showing how misallocation of inputs across firms can explain much of the cross-country productivity gap. It produced a large empirical literature on development and growth.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow are the central authors. Restuccia and Rogerson's closely related work (Rogerson is not credited here) was a parallel source. Restuccia is a defensible alternative.
assessment.maturity: Fifteen years of influence. The framework is standard, though the measurement details remain debated.
uncertainties: Sensitivity of measured misallocation to measurement error and to assumptions about markups.
Parallel contributions by Restuccia and Rogerson complicate attribution.
The most recent prize on growth and innovation (2025) may reduce near-term appetite.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic panel GMM estimators (Arellano–Bond, Arellano–Bover, Blundell–Bond) are routine tools in applied microeconomics, macroeconomics and finance, so the practical impact is very large. The contribution is methodological and enabling, in the tradition of the econometrics prizes.
assessment.attribution: The estimators carry the names of Arellano, Bond and Blundell, so the attribution is relatively clear. Bover, who co-authored one of the estimators, is not on the credited list. Blundell also has separate claims in labour and public economics.
assessment.maturity: More than thirty years of use, fully mature and well-understood.
uncertainties: Proliferating instruments and weak-instrument issues are known weaknesses of the methods.
Whether the Committee sees this as a refinement of GMM (Hansen, 2013 prize) rather than a new conceptual advance.
The omission of Bover from the credited list.
